# Plass

> Plass is a React UI component library published to npm as `plass-ui`. Behaviour and accessibility come from [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) primitives; styling comes from [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com) v4. It ships as ESM only with type declarations included, has one runtime dependency (`@base-ui/react`), and supports dark mode out of the box.

The design language: **a Plass surface is a key of tinted glass resting on a clear sheet.** Every surface answers one question — is this pressed, or does it hold something? A thing that is pressed is tinted glass: a two-stop gradient at 135° whose ends are the two ends of a colour family at one lightness (indigo to azure, vermilion to rose), a drop shadow **tinted with that family**, and a bloom of light that follows the pointer. There is deliberately no specular highlight and no inset edge on a filled control — a gradient that turns carries the form, and a highlight over the top of it reads as lacquer. A thing that holds something is clear glass: translucent, `blur(22px) saturate(160%)`, a white hairline round it, and never dyed. A control never moves — there is no `transform` on press — it answers in light and depth: `brightness(1.05)` on hover and `brightness(0.95)` on press, with the elevation going one step up and one step down.

`elevation` defaults to **1 on a PlButton and 0 on a PlTextField**: a key rests on the sheet, a field is cut into it.

Every component draws from one shared prop vocabulary, so `size="md"` means the same thing everywhere:

```ts
type PlassSize = 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl';
type PlassColor = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info';
type PlassDensity = 'default' | 'compact';
type PlassVariant = 'solid' | 'glass' | 'ghost';
type PlassElevation = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3;
```

`color` is one of six semantic families, never an arbitrary value like `#3558ef`. Setup is `npm install plass-ui`, then one line in the app's CSS entry point — `@import 'plass-ui/styles.css';`. That file ships compiled, so Tailwind is not a requirement on the consumer's side. A project that already runs Tailwind v4 imports `plass-ui/tailwind.css` instead, which is the token sheet and registers the package as a Tailwind source, so consumers never write an `@source` of their own.

**Version 0.0.1 is a preview.** Forty-five components are released, across six groups: display, feedback, inputs, layout, navigation and surfaces. Every component is exported under a `Pl` prefix — `PlButton`, `PlTextField`, `PlAccordion` — because the bare names are the most-taken identifiers in the ecosystem, and because the design language is meant to be portable to other toolkits. The shared prop vocabulary keeps the `Plass` prefix (`PlassSize`), and so do the CSS tokens (`--plass-*`).

Documentation is available in English (served from `/`) and Korean (served from `/ko/`). The links below are the English pages; prefix any path with `/ko` for the Korean version.

## Guide

- [Getting started](https://plass.cdget.com/guide/getting-started): Install, the one-line CSS setup, what the bundled reset does, the Tailwind path, the page wash the glass needs under it, first component, dark mode via `data-theme` or a class, browser support.
- [Design language](https://plass.cdget.com/design/design-language): The tinted-glass rule and everything that follows from it — the three layers of a filled surface, why the gradient turns instead of shading, the three-strength glass ladder, the one inset shadow, tinted shadows, brightness-based press, the pointer-following interaction light, the size and radius ladders, and the implementation rules.
- [Colour](https://plass.cdget.com/design/color): The six semantic families as gradient sweeps, the three hand-picked tokens per family, why a family's colour does not change with the theme, the measured contrast table (every stop within 0.15 of 4.5:1), and how to override a family.
- [Prop conventions](https://plass.cdget.com/design/prop-conventions): What the shared props mean, the naming rules a new component is checked against, and the three state props with their focus and native-attribute behaviour.

## Components

- [All components](https://plass.cdget.com/components/): Every released component on one page, each card a running preview rather than a picture.

### Display

- [PlList](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/list): A stack of rows — the list is a sheet, the rows are what is on it, and `size`/`density`/`dividers` are carried down by **context** rather than by `cloneElement`, which stops reaching a row the moment a caller `.map()`s their data. A row's shell is always an `<li>`; `onClick` or `href` puts a real `<button>` or `<a>` *inside* it, and `action` sits **outside** that pressable area, because a row that navigates and holds a toggle has two things to press. A chosen link gets `aria-current="page"`, a chosen button `aria-current="true"` — never `aria-pressed`, which would make it a toggle. `dividers` trades the sheet's padding and the rows' corners for edge-to-edge rules, drawn with `>li+li`. `role="list"` is written out because Tailwind's reset takes the bullets off and Safari takes the semantics with them. No Base UI primitive: a list is not a composite widget, and a listbox role on a page of links breaks a screen reader.
- [PlTable](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/table): A grid of data on a glass sheet. Takes `columns` and `rows` rather than markup, so the headings and the cells cannot drift apart; a column carries `key`, `header`, `width`, `align` and an optional `render`. `striped`, `hoverable`, `stickyHeader`, `caption`, `empty` and `onRowClick`. A clickable row keeps its `<tr>` semantics and gains a tab stop rather than a `role="button"`. Cell padding and alignment are inline styles, because host stylesheets style `td`/`th` by tag name at a specificity a utility class cannot outrank. It is generic in `Row` and so takes no `ref`.
- [PlAvatar](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/avatar): A picture of a person or a thing that is never an empty box, built on Base UI's Avatar — which owns the four-state load race. Three things can be drawn and one is at a time: the picture, then `children`/`initials`/initials derived from `name`, then a silhouette. The derivation is first-character-of-first-word plus first-of-last, and a single-token name gives one character, because two characters of a CJK name at 40px is a smudge. An avatar *is* the coloured thing, so its sheet takes the tint — but `variant` defaults to `ghost`, since a page of saturated circles is a page nobody can read a name off. `shape` is `circle` or the library's own fillet; there is no `density`. No status dot: that is a `PlBadge` with an avatar in it, and no `PlAvatarGroup` either — a stack is a negative margin and a ring.
- [PlBadge](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/badge): A small mark in the corner of something else — unread mail on an inbox icon, a status dot on an avatar. With `children` it wraps the anchor in an `inline-flex` shell that adds no width, so a badged icon button still lines up with a bare one; without them it lays out inline as a standalone status pill. A count of `0` draws nothing unless `showZero`, and a number past `max` is capped with a `+` (a word is left alone). Omitting `content` gives a dot; `dot` forces one while keeping the content for screen readers. `label` is what turns "3" into "3 unread notifications". Pulled out of the corner with a **negative margin**, never a `transform`; `overlap="circle"` adds the inset a round anchor needs. It is the one component allowed to be a pill — a badge is a mark laid on a surface, not a surface. No role, no tab stop, no Base UI primitive.
- [PlBlockquote](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/blockquote): Somebody else's words, set apart from your own — an accent rule down the leading edge, the quote at a heading's scale with a paragraph's leading. `author` is a person and `source` a work, because `<cite>` is for the title of a work and never for a name; passing either turns the wrapper into a `<figure>` with the `<figcaption>` **outside** the `<blockquote>`, since a name inside it claims the speaker said their own name. Without one the wrapper is a plain `<div>`. **Nothing is drawn on the `<blockquote>` element itself** — a host stylesheet's `blockquote` rule outranks a utility, so the surface, the rule and the padding all live on the wrapper. The sheet is never dyed; the family reaches the rule and stops. `ghost` is the default.
- [PlBreadcrumb](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/breadcrumb): The trail of pages above the one being read — a named `<nav>` around an `<ol>` (order is the meaning). The **last step is the current one** on its own: it takes `aria-current="page"` and stops being a link even with an `href`, and a step that claims it with `current` takes the mark off the last one, since only one element may carry it. A step is a real `<a>` with `href`, a real `<button>` with only `onClick`, and a `<span>` with neither. `maxItems` folds the middle behind a `…` that unfolds in place — but only when the fold actually removes more than one step. Four named `separator`s, because the difference is meaning; the two that point turn back under RTL. `structuredData` emits a `schema.org` BreadcrumbList beside the markup (off by default, since a page may have only one), with every step in it including the folded ones, made absolute by `baseUrl`. `PlBreadcrumbItem` inherits `size` from the trail.
- [PlChip](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/chip): A compact token — a tag, a filter, a status, an entity plucked out of a list. The shell is always a `<span>`; `onClick` puts a real `<button>` *inside* it and `onDelete` adds a second one, because a button inside a button is invalid HTML browsers un-nest on parse — so both are real, focusable, separately reachable. `aria-pressed` reports `selected`. A chip is one step **down** the control ladder (a `md` chip is a `sm` control, 32px), because a chip is a token inside a row rather than a control the row lines up against. `variant` defaults to `glass`: a row of gradient keys has no primary action. `selected` moves one step up the variant's own ladder — and on `solid`, which has no opacity ladder, it casts the tinted lift instead. `count` rides on its own plate.
- [PlDivider](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/divider): A rule between two things. Base UI's Separator, so a real `role="separator"` with the matching `aria-orientation`. Like `PlTextLink` it has **no default `color`** — left out, the rule is the neutral hairline, the one visible on a page wash, a glass sheet and a card alike; the sheet's own white hairline vanishes on anything opaque. `children` breaks the line around a label and `textAlign` decides where it sits, with a fixed stub on the near side rather than a flex ratio. A string label is copied into `aria-label`, because `separator` is not a name-from-content role. `length` rather than `width`, because the long axis turns with `orientation`. No `variant` and no `elevation`: a divider is not a surface.
- [PlHighlight](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/highlight): Marks the words a reader is looking for inside text they were already reading. The component *is* the search: `query` takes a string, an array (longest term tried first, or `['data','database']` would mark `data` and orphan `base`), or a `RegExp` (copied, never mutated, global forced on). `caseSensitive` and `wholeWord` are props, not pre-computed offsets; whole-word is checked with two character tests rather than a lookbehind, which Safari only grew in 16.4. `children` is a **tree** — elements are walked into and cloned, so a match inside a `<strong>` is marked and the `<strong>` survives. The mark is a real `<mark>`, so marking eleven words tells a screen reader eleven things matter. `color` defaults to `warning`, the one family light enough to be a highlighter. No `size`: a mark is the size of the text it is inside.
- [PlHotKeys](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/hot-keys): A keyboard key, a combination of them, or the four movement keys as an inverted-T `cluster`. `Mod` is the token the rest exist for — the only one whose *meaning* changes with the platform (⌘ on a Mac, Ctrl elsewhere); `os` overrides the detection for a page that must name a platform. Every glyph key carries its real name in a visually hidden box, because a screen reader announces `⌘` as "place of interest sign". The platform is resolved through `useSyncExternalStore` so a server-rendered page hydrates without a mismatch. `PlKbd` is exported as one cap. It displays a shortcut; it does not bind one.
- [PlIcon](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/icon): A glyph at a known size, in a known colour. The library ships no icon set — this gives whichever set the app chose the same two axes everything else has. The glyph is the `icon` **prop** rather than `children`, because size and colour are the two things you cannot reach once an icon set's element is a child. The box is `inline-flex` with `font-size` set to the same length as the box, so a px-authored `<svg>`, an em-authored one, a bare character and an `<img>` all come out the same size. `size` is its own 14/16/20/24/28px ladder, not the control heights. `color` defaults to **`inherit`**, the one component where it is not `primary`. Without `label` it is `aria-hidden` with no role; with one it is `role="img"` — there is no third case.
- [PlTimeline](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/timeline): A sequence of steps in the order they happen in, as a real `<ol>` — the order *is* the content. `active` is an **index**, not a value, because a timeline has no selection: everything before it is `complete`, the item at it is `current`, everything after `upcoming`. An item's index is never a prop; the timeline numbers its children as it walks them (through `Children.toArray`, so a conditional step that rendered nothing does not shift the count). Three states, three **axes** rather than three opacities: gradient, gradient plus a soft halo, hairline ring. The connector belongs to the item it *leaves*, so its colour says whether that step was reached, and it is one border edge so `dashed`/`dotted` are the browser's own. The current step takes `aria-current="step"`. `PlTimelineItem` inherits `size`/`density`/`orientation` and can override `status` and `color`.
- [PlTypography](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/typography): The library's type scale on its own — ten `level`s from `h1` to `overline`, each setting the size **and** the element it renders as. Deliberately not called `variant`, which in this library names what a surface is made of. There is no `size` either: `level` is the size, and a second axis would allow an `h1` at `xs`. `render` breaks the tie when the scale and the semantics have to differ. `weight` is resolved in JS so exactly one `font-*` class is ever emitted — two of equal specificity would be decided by stylesheet order. `color` has **no default** (text inherits the page's ink), and `caption`/`overline` are muted. `lines` truncates at 1 and line-clamps above it, leaving the whole string in the DOM. `gutter` is off: a component that injects margins is one a layout has to fight.
- [PlTextLink](https://plass.cdget.com/components/display/text-link): A link, in a sentence or on its own. No surface, no height, and — like nothing else in the library — **no default `color` and no default `size`**, because a link in a paragraph is the paragraph's colour with a line under it. `underline` is `'always' | 'hover' | 'none'` rather than a boolean. `newTab` sets `target`, merges `noopener noreferrer` into any `rel` the caller wrote, draws the external arrow and adds a visually hidden line for a screen reader. The component's class is doubled in CSS (`.plass-link.plass-link`) so a host page's `.prose a` cannot outrank it.

### Feedback

- [PlOverlay](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/overlay): A sheet over the whole page that stops it being used — the scrim on its own, with whatever the caller puts on top. Built on Base UI's Dialog, so the portal, scroll lock, focus trap, inert page and focus restoration are the primitive's. No `variant` (the page is already taken; `tone` is the real question) and no `elevation` (the overlay *is* the plane everything floats above). `tone` is one axis of legibility: `scrim` matches `PlModal`'s backdrop exactly so the two never seam, `glass` is a lighter dim over a real blur, `solid` is opaque, `clear` draws nothing and still catches the pointer. **`dismissible` is off by default** — the other way round from a modal, because an overlay is not asking a question, it is saying *wait*. `label` has a default, since an overlay holding only a spinner still has to name itself. Opacity is the only thing animated.
- [PlToast](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/toast): A message that appears on its own, says what happened, and leaves — `PlToastProvider` once around the app, `usePlToast` anywhere under it. A **hook, not a component**: what a caller has when a toast is warranted is a click handler, not a place in the tree. Built on Base UI's Toast, which owns the timers and their pausing on hover and window blur, the `limit` queue, the swipe, the F6 hotkey and the live region. Everything about how a toast looks lives on the provider so the call site is only *what happened*; `color`/`variant`/`icon` per toast ride in Base UI's `data` slot rather than shadowing manager option names. `position` is one word (`bottom-end`), never a side plus an align, because a stack is only ever pinned top or bottom. `timeout: 0` for anything the reader must act on. `update` with a reused id is one toast that changed its mind. `promise` follows a request through loading/success/error. The × is hidden from the a11y tree on purpose — F6 is the way in. No `elevation`: a toast always floats at shadow 3.
- [PlTooltip](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/tooltip): A short label that appears when the pointer rests on something, built on Base UI's Tooltip — the delay, the group timeout, opening on focus but not a click-focus, Escape, and collision handling are all the primitive's. The whole component is a wrapper: the Trigger merges onto the child, so it adds no element and no tab stop. The plate is the **same floating sheet as the `PlSelect` popup** (`--plass-glass-press`, white hairline, shadow 3), not the filled key most libraries draw — a tooltip is a note about something, and a second kind of floating sheet on one screen is one too many. It wires `role="tooltip"` and `aria-describedby` itself, dropping the reference while closed. `PlTooltipProvider` shares one delay across a toolbar. `color` defaults to `secondary`. A tooltip **describes, it does not name** — an icon-only button still needs its own `aria-label`.
- [PlProgressCircular](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/progress-circular): A ring that fills, for where there is no room for a bar. Takes `PlProgressLinear`'s props unchanged except `size`, which is diameter here rather than thickness — one component in three shapes is the claim, so they share a props table rather than three that would drift. The arc is the family's gradient rather than a flat colour, which costs a `<linearGradient>` of its own because an SVG stroke cannot be given a CSS one; the track under it is `--plass-track`, the same ink the bar's groove is. The value and the label sit **beside** the ring, not inside it: at `xs` the ring is fourteen pixels across and there is nowhere for "40%" to go. Indeterminate it draws a fixed quarter-arc and turns; with a value it holds still and the gap closes. The `<svg>` is `aria-hidden`, and under reduced motion the spin is slowed rather than stopped.
- [PlProgressLinear](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/progress-linear): A bar that fills, and the one indicator that shows *how much* is left at a glance. Built on Base UI's Progress, which owns `role="progressbar"`, the value and range attributes and `aria-valuetext`. The groove is `--plass-track` — the same neutral ink a `PlSlider`'s rail and a `PlSwitch`'s off track are cut in — and the segment over it is the family's gradient, so the filled run is the material the submit button is made of; the movement is on `width` because a gradient cannot be transitioned and a length can. No `variant`, no `density`, no `elevation`: one material, nothing to pad, and a groove does not float. `value` defaults to `null`, the indeterminate case, and the bar sweeps rather than sitting empty. `showValue` writes a percentage **of the range**, not of 100, unless `format` (`Intl.NumberFormatOptions`) says what the number means. Values outside the range are clamped. Under reduced motion the segment stops travelling and breathes in place rather than stopping.
- [PlSkeleton](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/skeleton): The shape of something that has not loaded yet — it reserves the space the real thing will take, which a spinner cannot. Three shapes sized off the ladders the real components use: a `line` is as tall as that step's type, a `circle` is exactly a `PlAvatar` at that size, a `rect` is a block. `lines` stacks real bars with real leading rather than one striped box, and draws the last one short the way a paragraph's last line is. Deliberately **not glass** — a flat tint with no blur, hairline, gloss or shadow, which also stops thirty placeholders asking for thirty backdrop filters. Unlabelled it is `aria-hidden`; `label` on the *one* that stands for the region makes it a `role="status"` with `aria-busy`. Under reduced motion the sweep becomes a colour pulse rather than stopping, since a still skeleton reads as an empty box that finished loading.
- [PlAlert](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/alert): A message about something that happened, set into the page it is about. An alert *is* the coloured thing, so its sheet takes the tint (unlike every container). `color` defaults to `info`, not `primary` — an alert is a note, not the primary anything. Each family draws its own shape as well as its own colour, so the severity does not depend on colour alone. `warning` and `danger` get `role="alert"`, the rest `role="status"`. The three shapes — bare line, line with glyph, headline plus detail — are one component with different slots filled. `onClose` is what makes the dismiss button appear; the component never hides itself.
- [PlModal](https://plass.cdget.com/components/feedback/modal): A sheet that takes the page away until it is answered, built on Base UI's Dialog — focus trap, scroll lock, aria wiring and focus restoration are all the primitive's. No `variant` and no `elevation`: a modal has already taken the page, and one that could be told to sit flat would be one that could be told to stop being a modal. `title` becomes the `<h2>`, `description` the accessible description, `actions` the end-aligned bottom row; `PlModalClose` is exported so an uncontrolled modal's Cancel button needs no state. The sheet caps its own height and scrolls only its body. Opening animates opacity alone.

### Inputs

- [PlButton](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/button): A control that runs an action. `variant` `size` `color` `density` `elevation`, plus `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `loading`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `fullWidth` and `render`. `elevation` defaults to 1; `solid` is a pane of tinted glass whose gradient turns in hue, `glass` wears the family in its label, `ghost` has no surface until hovered. Every variant carries `.plass-glow`, a bloom that follows the pointer and flashes on press.
- [PlButtonGroup](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/button-group): A run of buttons that belong together. The corners that face a neighbour are squared off with logical properties, and `variant` `size` `color` `density` `elevation` `disabled` are stated once for the set — a group where one button is a size out is the failure it exists to prevent. The axes carry **no defaults of their own**: an axis the group does not state is one each button falls back to its own default on, and a button that states one itself still wins. Inheritance travels by context rather than by `cloneElement`, so it reaches a button wrapped in a tooltip, a fragment or a `.map()`. Only `glass` overlaps its keys by a pixel, because it is the only variant that draws an edge and two hairlines meeting is a seam twice the weight of every other line on the page. `orientation` and `fullWidth`. It is **not** a segmented control and has no value — that is `PlSegmentedButton`, which carries the roving focus and `radiogroup` semantics.
- [PlTextField](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/text-field): Single- or multi-line text input. The label, the description and the error are part of the component, wired together by Base UI's Field. `variant` defaults to `glass`; `solid` is a well cut into the sheet rather than a tinted pane, because a gradient under a caret is not legible. `error` also turns the field invalid, which re-points the whole slot family at `danger`.
- [PlCheckbox](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/checkbox): A single yes/no, built on Base UI's Checkbox. Clear glass with a hairline until ticked, then the family's gradient — the one place the library expresses a state by swapping the whole surface rather than shifting a step, because on and off are not two strengths of one material. No `variant`. The tick has its own size and radius ladders (`tickSizeClasses`, `tickRadiusClasses`), because a radius sized for a 40px control turns an 18px box into a circle. `label`/`description`/`error` from Base UI's Field; `indeterminate` gives the third state and `aria-checked="mixed"`.
- [PlFilePicker](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/file-picker): A box you drop files on, or click to open the file dialog. No Base UI primitive — a dropzone is a div listening for four drag events plus an `<input type="file">`. It gets right the two things hand-rolled dropzones miss: a drag *depth counter* (dragenter/dragleave fire per child, so a boolean flickers) and applying `accept` to drops (the browser enforces it on its own dialog only). `maxFiles` counts against what is already held. `onReject` reports every refusal with a reason — `type`, `size` or `count`. The dashed edge is the one non-solid line in the library. `formatFileSize` is exported alongside it.
- [PlNumberField](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/number-field): A field that only holds a number, built on Base UI's NumberField — locale-aware parsing, clamping, press-and-hold repeat on the steppers and the hidden form input are all the primitive's. The shell is a `PlTextField`'s **to the pixel** (`fieldRestClasses`), so a quantity box in a form is the same object as the boxes around it, and `solid` is the well rather than a tinted pane. `steppers` is `end`, `split` or `none`; there is deliberately no stacked pair of half-height chevrons, because at `xs` each arrow would be under three pixels tall. `format` goes straight to `Intl.NumberFormat`, so the field can show `$1,240.00` while `value` stays `1240`. Shift takes `largeStep`, Alt `smallStep`. `allowWheelScrub` is off by default. `error` re-points the whole slot family at `danger`.
- [PlPagination](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/pagination): The strip of page numbers under a long list. Every button is a real `PlButton`, so it inherits the surface, the press signature and the height ladder. `count`, `page`/`defaultPage`, `onPageChange`, `siblingCount`, `boundaryCount`, `showArrows`, `showEdges`. The slot count stays constant as the window slides, and a one-page gap is filled with the page rather than an ellipsis. `getPageHref` turns every number into a real `<a href>` a crawler can follow; a handler alongside it cancels the navigation for a client-side router. Renders a `<nav>` around a `<ul>` with `aria-current="page"` and a live-region status line.
- [PlRadioGroup](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/radio-group): A set of options where exactly one is chosen, built on Base UI's RadioGroup — the set takes one tab stop and the arrow keys move within it. `PlRadioGroup` holds the set and `PlRadio` is one option; `size`, `color` and `readOnly` are inherited from the group, because a radio says nothing on its own. The dot is round, one of only two round things in the library. `orientation` defaults to `vertical`.
- [PlSegmentedButton](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/segmented-button): Two or more choices in one pill, exactly one taken. Built on Base UI's RadioGroup — `role="radiogroup"`, one tab stop, arrow keys, `aria-checked` — because a segmented button *is* "exactly one of these"; `aria-pressed` toggles would announce four independent switches. The groove carries `--plass-well`; on `solid` the tile is the family's gradient with its tinted lift, a key riding in a groove. The tile animates `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` measured off the chosen segment rather than a `transform`, so no label is resampled while it moves, and it is not mounted until something is chosen so the first choice appears in place. `PlSegment` inherits `variant`, `size` and `density` from the set.
- [PlSelect](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/select): One value chosen from a list, built on Base UI's Select. The trigger is drawn on `PlTextField`'s shell (`fieldRestClasses` in `internal/styles.ts`), so a select and a field in the same form are the same object; `solid` is the well, not a tinted pane. Options are `items` (data, not children) because the trigger has to know the labels before the popup opens. `label`/`description`/`error` come from Base UI's Field; `error` re-points the family at `danger`. The trigger is held open at the width of its longest label so choosing a shorter option does not shrink it. The popup is portalled and its positioner carries `.plass-portal`.
- [PlSlider](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/slider): A value chosen along a range, built on Base UI's Slider. The rail is a groove carrying `--plass-well` — the same inset shadow a `solid` field is drawn with — and the filled run is the family's gradient, with the thumb ringed in `--plass-surface` so it never dissolves into it. An array `value` makes it a range slider; there is no `range` prop. No `variant`: a slider is a groove and a key at once, and neither has a choice to offer. `label`, `description`, `showValue` (a function gets Base UI's localised strings), `orientation`.
- [PlSwitch](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/switch): An immediate on/off, built on Base UI's Switch. Off, the track is the groove carrying `--plass-well`; on, it is the family's gradient with its tinted lift. The thumb keeps `--plass-surface` in both states — it is the light on the track, not a second coloured object — and it is the one thing in the library that moves. No `variant`. `labelPlacement` puts the label before the track for a settings list. Choose it over `PlCheckbox` when the change takes effect immediately; if there is a Save button underneath, it should have been a checkbox.

- [PlIconButton](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/icon-button): A round button with a glyph in it and nothing else. It **is** a `PlButton` — the three materials, the elevation ladder, the pointer light, `loading`, `readOnly`, `disabled` and `render` all pass through untouched — with `children`/`startIcon`/`endIcon` replaced by one `icon`. Two things differ. `label` is **required**, because a button whose whole label is a drawing has no accessible name at all and "an icon button with no `aria-label`" is the commonest accessibility defect a component library ships; making it required is the only fix that survives review. And the shape is a disc, a deliberate exception to the house radius rule: that rule protects the flat run along the top and bottom edge where a line of text sits, and a glyph has no line of text, so a circle with one mark centred in it says the same thing by a different route. The radius is an inline style rather than a `rounded-full`, because PlButton already writes a `rounded-*` utility and two utilities setting one property resolve by stylesheet order.
- [PlRating](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/rating): A score out of five as a row of stars. An interactive one is a real **radio group** of hidden `<input type="radio">`s, one per choosable score under the fraction of a star it stands for — a rating *is* "exactly one of these", so it gets one tab stop, arrow keys, `aria-checked`, and a value in a form submission, none of which a row of buttons has. `precision` bounds what can be **chosen** and nothing else: a `value` of `4.3` draws as four stars and a third at every precision, because an average is not a choice. The fraction is the filled star laid over the empty one and clipped by width — nothing transformed, nothing scaled, so a half star is the left half of exactly the star beside it, and the clip runs from the inline start so it fills from the right under RTL. `readOnly` is a different component in the same clothes: no inputs at all, one `role="img"` with the score as a sentence, and it is the one `readOnly` in the library that does not drain the saturation — a row of grey stars would say the score itself was unavailable. Clearing rides on `click`, not `change`, because clicking an already-checked radio fires no change. `color` defaults to `warning`, the one place a component's default colour is chosen by what the object is rather than by what it means.
- [PlOtpField](https://plass.cdget.com/components/inputs/otp-field): A row of one-character slots — a PIN, a texted verification code, an invite key — built on Base UI's OTP Field, which owns one hidden value behind however many inputs, paste spread across the slots from wherever the caret was, backspace stepping back a box, a click landing on the first empty slot, and `autocomplete="one-time-code"` so a phone offers the code from the message. `length` is clamped to 2–12: one box is a `PlTextField` and past twelve the row stops fitting a phone. `charset` (`numeric` by default, because that is what a texted code is and what puts a number pad on a phone) drops what it rejects rather than showing it, and reports through `onValueInvalid`. `groupSize`/`separator` split the row, and the separator is an `aria-hidden` span rather than a `role="separator"` — punctuation inside one value, not a break between two things. A slot has its own size, radius and type ladders: taller than it is wide so a row reads as places for one character each, a radius measured against the slot's *width* rather than a control's height (or `md` would be a pill), and type two steps up the control ladder, because a code is read off one phone and typed with the other hand. The shell is `PlTextField`'s, so `solid` is the well and not a tinted pane. The focus ring is `:focus` rather than `:focus-visible`, the one place in the library that distinction is deliberately dropped.

### Layout

- [PlAspectRatio](https://plass.cdget.com/components/layout/aspect-ratio): A box that keeps a proportion whatever width it is given, and draws nothing at all — no sheet, no hairline, no shadow. `ratio` is CSS's own `aspect-ratio` untranslated, so a number or a `'16 / 9'` reaches the property as written. `fit` is the one convenience on top: a direct `img`, `video`, `canvas`, `svg` or `picture` is stretched to the box and then fitted, which is the pair of declarations every use would otherwise start with — an `iframe` takes the sizing and not the fit, because an embed lays its own content out. `rounded` cuts the corners to the `size` step of the house ladder, and the box clips either way, since a `cover` image that spilled out of its proportion would leave the component reserving space rather than holding anything to it. The only shared axis is `size`, and it is the size of the sheet: a layout component that drew a surface would make a proportion a visual decision.

- [PlContainer](https://plass.cdget.com/components/layout/container): Horizontal breathing room and optionally a measure, drawing nothing itself — the outermost element on a page is the one thing that must not decide what the page looks like. `maxWidth` is the breakpoint ladder in `rem` (`xs` 30 · `sm` 40 · `md` 48 · `lg` 64 · `xl` 80) rather than a framework's own container scale, so a container's `lg` and an `lg:` utility change at the same width; `none` is the default, because the gutter is the job and a measure is a second decision. The gutter is the **sheet** padding track, not the control one: what is inside is a page, and a page's margin from the window is a card's margin round a paragraph. `padded={false}` gives the gutter up and keeps the measure and the centring, which is what a container nested in one that already pads wants. `centered` is inert while `maxWidth` is `none` — with no measure there is nothing left over to centre in. It has nothing to do with the grid: a container holds one as happily as it holds a paragraph, and a grid needs no container around it.
- [PlGrid](https://plass.cdget.com/components/layout/grid): A twelve-column row (`PlGrid`) and the cells in it (`PlGridItem`), drawing nothing — no sheet, no padding, no typography, and no `variant`/`color`/`elevation`/`size`/`density` on either. `span`, `offset`, `columns` and the three spacings are all `PlassResponsive<T>`: a bare value applies everywhere, a map applies each entry from its own breakpoint up, and the breakpoints are Tailwind's own so a Plass grid and an `md:` utility change together. A span wider than the row is clamped to it rather than overflowing; `offset` is space pushed in **ahead** of a cell rather than an absolute position, so document order stays reading order. `spacing` is Tailwind's scale (`4` is `1rem`, fractions allowed) and the gutter comes out of the cell, so two halves plus one gutter is exactly the row. It is a flex row with a percentage width per cell, not `display: grid` — the only shape where a cell can carry a start offset with no line number and where the row can be told not to wrap. The column count and both gutters reach a cell as **inherited custom properties** rather than through context, because a media query can change one without React hearing about it; the width arithmetic itself is real CSS in `styles.css`, since a class name assembled at runtime is one Tailwind never sees. Nesting is a grid inside a *cell*.
- [PlPanes](https://plass.cdget.com/components/layout/panes): A set of regions (`PlPane`) with draggable handles between them, sized in **fractions** written as `flex-basis: calc((100% − gutters) × fraction)` — which is the decision the whole component follows from: a split described as a percentage survives a window resize with nothing running, so it measures itself only twice, on mount and at the start of each drag. That measurement is a `ResizeObserver` rather than one read, because a split inside a closed accordion is zero wide when it mounts. `defaultSize`/`minSize`/`maxSize` take a number as a percentage and a string as an absolute length (`'240px'`), and they are read by the **split** rather than the pane — a pane cannot know what "half" is. Handles are interleaved by the component, so the children are just panes; what is drawn is a hairline and what can be **grabbed** is a track around it, the same split a scrollbar makes. A handle is a `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow`, a tab stop while `resizable`, and moved by the arrow keys — a key press fires `onResizeEnd` because it is a whole gesture on its own. A drag takes the page's text selection away (as `-webkit-user-select`, the only name WebKit implements) rather than calling `preventDefault`, which would stop the browser focusing the handle; and it tears itself down on unmount, because the `pointerup` that would have ended it never arrives after a route change.

### Navigation

- [PlBottomNavigation](https://plass.cdget.com/components/navigation/bottom-navigation): A row of destinations held against the bottom edge of the window. A `<nav>` of real links or buttons and deliberately **not** a `role="tablist"`: a tab list owes a keyboard reader one tab stop and arrow keys, and a screen reader a panel per tab, and a bottom navigation switches what the *page* is — claiming the role without the behaviour is worse than never claiming it. What it claims instead is `aria-current="page"`, never `aria-pressed`. `position` defaults to `fixed`, against the `static` a layout component takes, because that is what this component is; only a `static` bar has corners, since one spanning a window edge has nothing behind them. `labels` (`all` · `selected` · `none`) never changes the bar's height — the named item is always the tallest — and an **undrawn name is still in the document**, because a glyph on its own has no accessible name. `safeArea` moves the items clear of the home indicator while the sheet keeps reaching the bottom of the screen, so no stripe of page shows under the glass. The sheet is never dyed; the family is carried by the one item that is current. An item with an `href` is a real `<a>` (long-press, status bar, crawler) and loses that `href` when disabled, since `disabled` is not a state an `<a>` can be in.
- [PlFloatingBottomNavigation](https://plass.cdget.com/components/navigation/floating-bottom-navigation): A row of round destinations floating clear of the bottom edge — a capsule of clear glass with a key of tinted glass riding in it. The other half of `PlBottomNavigation` and a separate component rather than a `floating` boolean, because half the props on each would mean nothing on the other: that bar is *attached* to the window edge (full width, a hairline against the content, flat), and this one is not part of the page at all, which is where the capsule, the gap, the `elevation` of **2** and the pill corners all come from. `rounded-full` is one of the very few pills the library allows, for the reason a segmented button's groove is: the house fillet is about a sheet with its corners cut, and a sheet that is not on anything has no corners to cut. Every destination is a disc with a glyph and **no name drawn** — the name is required and lives in a clipped box, because a row of glyphs with no accessible names is the defect `PlIconButton`'s `label` exists to prevent. The strip the capsule is centred in spans the window and takes no pointer events; only the capsule takes them back, or a transparent band would swallow every press along the bottom of the page. The focus ring on a disc is offset rather than flush, the one place in the library that differs: a flush ring on a circle is the circle's own edge thickening.
- [PlMenu](https://plass.cdget.com/components/navigation/menu): A list of actions that appears when something is pressed, built on Base UI's Menu — the `menu`/`menuitem` roles, roving focus, typeahead, `Esc`, outside-click, focus restored to the trigger, and submenus that open on hover with a safe triangle. The rows are **composed, not passed as data** — the opposite of `PlSelect`, and deliberately: a select's options are values a caller already has, a menu's rows are code, and data would mean an `items` type with a variant per row shape. `PlMenuItem` renders a real `<a>` when given an `href`; `PlMenuCheckboxItem` (tick) and `PlMenuRadioItem` (dot) both default to **staying open**, against a plain row's `closeOnClick`. A row's `color` is a *branch* rather than an appended class, because two utilities of equal specificity resolve by stylesheet order and an appended accent would silently do nothing. Rows carry no focus ring — Base UI moves focus onto the highlighted row, so the tint is the indicator and `data-highlighted` is what lights it, which makes the keyboard and the pointer light the same row. The popup is `PlSelect`'s popup to the pixel and animates **opacity only**: a menu that slides in has moved the row you were reaching for. There is no `variant` (a popup that took the pointer has already answered that question) and no `elevation` (it is fixed at 3, because a menu genuinely floats). `PlContextMenu` is the same surface opened by a right-click or a long press, taking the rows as `content` and the region as `children`.

### Surfaces

- [PlCard](https://plass.cdget.com/components/surfaces/card): The sheet everything else on a screen is grouped onto. `title`, `subtitle`, `headerAction`, `footer` and the body are slots rather than sub-components. `elevation` defaults to 1 — a card lies on the page wash. `dividers` scores the sheet instead of spacing its sections; `padded={false}` gives up the inset for full-bleed content; `interactive` lifts the sheet under the pointer, which is the one `transform` in the library, allowed because a card holds content rather than being pressed. It adds no role — a clickable card takes a real element through `render`.
- [PlChatBubble](https://plass.cdget.com/components/surfaces/chat-bubble): One message in a conversation. `side` is `start`/`end`, never them/me or left/right, and it decides only the row direction and which corner is cut short — a flat **4px** written out rather than a step down the radius ladder, because 8px against 16px is not a difference anyone reads as meaning something. That cut is the library's one piece of chat vocabulary: it does a tail's job without hanging a triangle off a sheet cut with a straight edge. A bubble *is* the coloured thing, so `solid` floods it — and `variant` is deliberately **not** tied to `side`, since which column is filled is a product decision. Five delivery states, of which only `read` and `failed` carry colour; the mark is drawn and the word lives in a clipped box. `typing` swaps in three dots that change colour without moving, leaving `children` intact. `media` is edge-to-edge (the padding lives on the sections), and the link card's surface is mixed from `currentColor` so it works on a filled bubble and a bare one alike. `actions` fade in on hover or focus, and are always visible on touch. No role of its own: the thread is the page's list.
- [PlTabs](https://plass.cdget.com/components/surfaces/tabs): One set of panels, one of which is shown, built on Base UI's Tabs — roving focus, the arrow keys on the bar's own axis, the `tab`/`tabpanel` roles and the `aria-controls` wiring. `PlTab` and `PlTabPanel` are written as siblings and sorted apart by the component; there is no `PlTabList` to remember. `activateOnFocus` is off by default, because automatic activation fires a request per tab walked past once a panel fetches. `variant` `glass` is the classic rule-and-indicator bar; `solid` is a groove with a **clear** pane in it, deliberately not the gradient — that tile belongs to `PlSegmentedButton`. The indicator animates `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` from Base UI's `--active-tab-*`, never a transform.
- [PlAccordion](https://plass.cdget.com/components/surfaces/accordion): A stack of sections that fold open one at a time, built on Base UI's Accordion. `PlAccordion` holds the stack and `PlAccordionItem` is one fold; `size`, `density` and `dividers` are inherited from the stack rather than set per item. `variant` defaults to `glass` and is read the way a container reads it — `solid` is the densest clear glass, never a tinted pane, because a sheet holds other people's content and is never dyed. `multiple` lets more than one stay open; `dividers` (on by default) scores the pane instead of tiling it. The panel animates its height from Base UI's measured `--accordion-panel-height`.
